_about: Papers waiting to be built. Agents: pick yours by batch, follow CLAUDE.md, and remove nothing from this file.

papers.hint: Train a deep plain net vs the same net with skip connections live (tiny MLP in JS on a 2D toy task); show the deep plain net's loss stalling while the residual one trains, plus gradient size per layer.
Fit a small net to a few noisy 2D points with and without dropout; watch the overfit decision boundary vs the smoother one, and see random neurons switch off each step.
Race SGD, momentum, RMSProp and Adam on a 2D loss surface the visitor can pick (ravine, saddle, noisy); click to set the start point; show trajectories and the per-parameter step sizes Adam adapts.
Train skip-gram on a tiny built-in corpus in the browser; show 2D projected word vectors moving as training runs, and let the visitor try analogies like king - man + woman.

1D or 2D GAN training live: generator samples vs real data distribution, discriminator's decision curve; visitor can change the real distribution and watch the generator chase it (and see mode collapse).
2D point-cloud diffusion: visitor draws a shape, forward process noises it step by step, a small pre-computed or live-trained denoiser reverses it; scrub the timestep slider.
Compare an MLP (fixed activations on nodes) with a KAN (learnable splines on edges) fitting a 1D/2D function; show each edge's learned spline and let visitor drag spline control points.
Selective state space: a sequence scrolls past a hidden state; toggle selectivity on/off and see how input-dependent gating lets the model keep or forget tokens on a copying / selective-recall task.
A tiny policy on a 1D/2D task; show the probability ratio and the clipped objective; slider for epsilon; compare clipped vs unclipped updates exploding on the same batch.

2D 'flatland' NeRF: render a 1D image from a 2D scene by marching rays through a density/color field; visitor moves the camera and sees volume rendering accumulate along each ray; optionally fit a tiny field to a few views.

A 2D robot end-effector must push a block around an obstacle where demos go left OR right; show that a regression (mean) policy averages into the obstacle while a diffusion policy samples one valid mode.
